decisions.reason: Although it was publicly launched, this generic utility web service sits at the edge of the firm's regulated-energy platform strategy, so its likely modest sunk cost makes withdrawal easier than continued commitment.

Because the Austrian gas grid fee database is close to the firm's core data business, management can justify continued support as a strategic extension and read any weak uptake as a temporary market-development issue.

The peak load window determination service uses the firm's analytical strengths in regulated energy processes and fits the announced end-to-end digital model, which favors persistence after the initial investment.
An end-customer tariff database offered as a product line with several models signals higher development effort and visible commitment, so escalation-of-commitment logic strongly favors keeping it.
Custom web services align with the firm's existing mix of software and operational services, giving management a strong basis to keep backing them rather than admit an early misstep.
This postal code lookup service appears less central to the firm's differentiated energy-market offering, so the firm has fewer strategic and reputational reasons to keep committing resources to it.
